target.title: fix(gateway): cap sessions.list limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `sessions.list` gateway RPC accepts an unbounded `limit`. The shipped `sessions_list` agent tool (`src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts:175`) reads `limit` via `readPositiveIntegerParam` (no maximum) and forwards it straight to the RPC, so any model invocation can pass `limit: 1e12`. The handler side resolves it in `resolveSessionsListLimit` (`src/gateway/session-utils.ts:2480`) with only a lower bound (`Math.max(1, Math.floor(opts.limit))`), and the protocol schema (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions.ts:217`) declares `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` with no maximum. A pathological limit forces a full session-store scan plus row materialization for every entry on a single request.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirrors the merged clamp pattern from #110552: add a named `SESSIONS_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 1000` const next to `SESSIONS_LIST_DEFAULT_LIMIT` and clamp inside `resolveSessionsListLimit` with `Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(opts.limit)), SESSIONS_LIST_MAX_LIMIT)`. Clamp-only, deliberately no TypeBox schema change — same shape as #110552, which avoids the stricter-validation merge risk of rejecting previously-accepted params. Callers passing larger values still get a successful response with a bounded window; `limitApplied` in the payload reports the effective limit.

## User Impact

Pathological `limit` values (e.g. `1e12` from an agent tool call) are now capped at 1000 rows instead of scanning and materializing the entire session store in one request. Normal usage (limit ≤ 1000, or the 100-row default) is unchanged. No config, schema, or API contract change.

## Evidence

- Test: `src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts` — new test `sessions.list caps pathological limit values` seeds a 1001-entry store, calls `sessions.list` with `limit: 1e12`, and asserts `limitApplied === 1000`, `count === 1000`, `totalCount === 1001` via the real RPC handler.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts` — 7/7 passed (6 existing + 1 new).
- Reverse verification: with the production change stashed, the new test fails (`limitApplied` is uncapped); with the change restored, 7/7 pass.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` — no errors attributable to this change.
- `git diff --check` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on both touched files.
- Diff stat: `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` +6/-1, `src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts` +22/-0 (2 files, 27 insertions, 1 deletion).

Follows the pattern precedent #110552.


**Contract precedent (round 2):** the 1000 ceiling aligns `sessions.list` with the gateway's existing list-cap family rather than introducing a new contract — `sessions-history-http.ts:49` (`MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT = 1000`, same session domain, same clamp-not-reject shape), `server-plugins.ts:358` (`PLUGIN_SUBAGENT_SESSION_MESSAGES_MAX_LIMIT = 1_000`), plus `tasks.ts` (500), `operator-approval-store.ts` (100/1001), and `cron-list-caller-scope.ts` (200). Clamped responses stay schema-valid and self-describing (`limitApplied`/`hasMore`/`nextOffset`); added compatibility coverage proves `offset: nextOffset` continues into the exact remainder (`hasMore: false`), so paginating callers are unaffected and non-paginating callers get a valid first page plus a machine-readable truncation signal — identical to the shipped session-history cap behavior.
